summary_paragraph: A woman with prior Roux-en-Y gastric bypass complicated by post-surgical malabsorption and hypoglycemia requiring continuous gastrostomy tube feeds was admitted to the bariatric surgery service for recurrent severe pain at the G-tube site after running out of oxycodone at home and being unable to control symptoms with acetaminophen; she briefly used naproxen with relief but stopped due to high marginal-ulcer risk. Exam showed a clean G-tube site without erythema or induration and a soft, non-distended abdomen; labs were reassuring and she remained afebrile and hemodynamically stable without evidence of infection or bleeding. She continued her home continuous tube feeds with monitoring, received DVT prophylaxis, and her pain was managed with oral oxycodone with short-term IV hydromorphone for breakthrough, then transitioned to oral-only therapy prior to discharge. She was discharged home ambulatory and stable with instructions to resume NutriHep continuous feeds at 45 cc/hr, monitor blood sugars, avoid NSAIDs, continue home medications, use PRN oxycodone safely, and follow up with her surgeon and planned specialty evaluations.
